name: Arga Labs

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: 10 pre-built digital twins/month; 1 twin per run; fixed 10-minute run sessions; community support. Docs describe the same tier as 10 URL Test Runs/month.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Flat $1,250/month (not a usage credit). 1,500 twin runs/month, 30,000 long-running twin minutes/month, 1,500 CI checks/month (separate, non-fungible buckets); unlimited app twins; long-running scenarios, test runner, saved tests; community support. Overage terms not published.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: From $3,500/month, adjusted by usage & team size; unlimited twins, twin runs, long-running twin minutes and CI checks; SOC 2 compliance (listed); onboarding + priority support; Twin Run TTL up to 480 min.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom pricing; permanent scenarios; scoped team roles & access; custom infra changes; on-prem hosting if requested; SSO/access controls; auditability; dedicated forward deployed engineer.

caveats: Free 10 twins/mo and 10min runs; Pro $1250/mo with 1500 runs, 30k long-running twin minutes, 1500 CI checks; Team from $3500 quote-adjusted, Enterprise custom/on-prem. Not a raw 4/8 sandbox rate; stateful API twins have different units.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Docs plans page (Free/Team/Paid: Team 500 PR Test Runs + 500 CI checks) disagrees with the pricing page (Free/Pro/Team/Enterprise: Pro 1,500 twin runs + 1,500 CI checks). Pricing page used as the authority.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

fleet.verification: Self-serve Free and Pro via app checkout (Settings > Upgrade subscription); Team/Enterprise via demo call.
fleet.tiers: Free: 1 twin per run, 10 twins/month, 10-min TTL. Pro: 1,500 twin runs + 30,000 long-running twin minutes + 1,500 CI checks per month. Team (from $3,500) and Enterprise: unlimited.
fleet.notes: Card has no fleet block. No concurrency limit is published for Twin Runs; limits are monthly run/minute counts. Twins are API replicas, not VMs.

snapshot_auto.quote: Arga provisions the service environment. Your application continues to run wherever you deploy it: locally, in staging, or at an existing preview URL. PR Test Runs do not create a new application sandbox for every pull request.
snapshot_auto.note: No user machine exists: Arga hosts API 'digital twins' (stateful service emulators) plus a hosted browser test runner; your app runs elsewhere. Twin Runs expire at TTL (max 480 min) and state is not auto-saved; persistent twin environments are attached to a Scenario and can be reseeded.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Arga provisions the service environment. Your application continues to run wherever you deploy it: locally, in staging, or at an existing preview URL. PR Test Runs do not create a new application sandbox for every pull request.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No machine snapshots. Closest analog (service state, not a machine): twin dashboards have a 'Save scenario' button that "captures the twin's current state as a `seed_config` payload" (docs.argalabs.com/features/custom-scenarios.md), and new Twin Runs can be seeded from that Scenario. No memory/process state; how-it-works says Arga "does not ... reconstruct the application's process state".

own_agent_api.quote: Starts a browser Test Run from a natural-language prompt.
own_agent_api.note: Drives Arga's OWN hosted browser QA agent only (not Claude Code/Codex etc., and not inside a user sandbox): POST /runner/runs with a prompt, WEBSOCKET /runner/runs/{run_id}/stream ("Streams run events"), POST /runner/runs/{run_id}/messages ("Append instructions to a running runner run"), list/get/rerun runs, saved tests; also CLI, MCP and Python/TS SDKs. Borderline: it is a test agent, not a general harness.

harness_api.quote: Starts a browser Test Run from a natural-language prompt.
harness_api.note: Drives Arga's OWN hosted browser QA agent only (not Claude Code/Codex etc., and not inside a user sandbox): POST /runner/runs with a prompt, WEBSOCKET /runner/runs/{run_id}/stream ("Streams run events"), POST /runner/runs/{run_id}/messages ("Append instructions to a running runner run"), list/get/rerun runs, saved tests; also CLI, MCP and Python/TS SDKs. Borderline: it is a test agent, not a general harness.

egress_allowlist.quote: Arga provisions the service environment. Your application continues to run wherever you deploy it: locally, in staging, or at an existing preview URL. PR Test Runs do not create a new application sandbox for every pull request.
egress_allowlist.note: No user machine; your app runs in your own environment. Twins 'intercept' provider hostnames (e.g. api.stripe.com) only by you swapping base URLs/env vars, not a provider-side egress control.

ingress_rules.quote: Revokes public `pub-` host access for a provisioned twin environment. Private proxy-token access remains available until TTL or teardown.
ingress_rules.note: Applies to twin endpoints (not user machines): POST /validate/twins/provision takes `public` (default true: "Whether returned base URLs are public drop-in hosts"); /lock switches a running Twin Run to private proxy-token access only. No IP allowlists documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Arga provisions the service environment. Your application continues to run wherever you deploy it: locally, in staging, or at an existing preview URL. PR Test Runs do not create a new application sandbox for every pull request.
guest_firewall.note: No guest machine is provided to the user.

secret_proxy.quote: For most twins, the `Authorization` header is stripped from proxied requests because the twin doesn't need real credentials
secret_proxy.note: Not a credential-injection proxy: twins replace real services and hand out fake twin tokens (e.g. xoxb-... for Slack) that you put in your .env; no real secret reaches anywhere. Saved Tests can store 'optional encrypted credentials' for the browser runner (validate-modes.md). No user sandbox.
